newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's forint flat vs dlr, firms vs NBH basket.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's forint flat vs dlr, firms vs NBH basket.

text.p: The forint was unchanged against the dollar at Friday's closing but firmed versus the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) currency basket, dealers said.
The forint finished a lacklustre session at 185.95/186.00 to the dollar, unchanged from its opening.

The Hungarian currency weakened by the mark's slight losses versus the dollar, but the forint moved towards the NBH's resistance level (bid) and closed 10 fillers below it, compared with a 20 filler differential in early trading.
Dealers said the forint was likely to return to the NBH bid where it usually trades although a recent fall in interest rates may have contributed to its easing.
The main factor which drove the forint to some 20 fillers below the NBH bid on Thursday was that banks' clients had import bills to pay in foreign currencies at the end of the month, dealers said.

"These were probably gas (import) bills," said Peter Sipos of BNP-Dresdner Bank, adding that the fall of forint interest rates made the forint less attractive relative to foreign currencies than earlier and small currency purchases were able to push the forint down.

Inter-Europa Bank's Peter Luczo said several foreign investors may have taken profits and sold forints after a fall in government securities yields after the announcement earlier this week that Hungary will cut the monthly rate of forint devaluation to one percent on August 15 from 1.1 percent.
The NBH's intervention band is 4.5 percent wide. The forint floats against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
